CLOSURE_MOD_EVENT_RHODES_ISLAND_WORKSHOP: In a maintenance corridor aboard Rhodes Island, you find a door left ajar. Stickers nearly cover its nameplate: Engineering Workshop. A newer note reads: Admission: 42 gold. No credit. Nobody is inside. The terminal glows among half-disassembled devices, and exactly 42 gold sits in the return slot.
You take the coins from the return slot. The unlocked drawers beneath the workbench are tempting, but you turn away. Better not rummage through someone else's things. Gain 42 gold.

Further inside, the workshop looks less and less like a place used only for repairs. Discontinued parts line the shelves, unknown device shells fill a corner, and old shipping labels cover several boxes. Two drawers beneath the workbench are partly open.

The drawer is packed with curious things. Some look valuable; others have long lost their original purpose. Two items stand out: an extravagantly ornate old cheque book and a remarkably well-preserved gift card.
Your gold can go as low as -100.
Shop items are discounted more often.

This drawer is much tidier than the other. A small mechanical giraffe and a carefully polished scope rest on soft padding. Both have clearly been used for a long time, yet both have been kept in excellent condition.
Once per combat, Block can fully prevent excess damage.
At the start of each turn, gain 10% damage for this combat.

The cheque book gleams with metal ornament and silver-edged paper. The banks and country that once honored it are gone, yet Closure has kept it carefully. A note beneath it reads: Just because it cannot be cashed does not mean it has no value.

The card's edges are worn, but its back is packed with discounts, dates, rules, and calculations. One line is circled three times: If the discount is deep enough, buying things does not count as spending money. A tiny special-offer clause has several stars beside it. On the back, almost erased: The more discounts, the better.

A palm-sized mechanical giraffe stands in the drawer. Its delicate joints adjust as you press it, distributing the force until it stands steady again. An inscription reads: Before the energy runs out, carry all things beyond the wilderness. As you lift it, tiny gears turn and its legs seek their balance once more.

The lens is spotless. Years of tiny marks on the housing have never impaired its precision. Through it, the workshop falls away until only one distant point remains. Lock the target, hold steady, and break resistance for a future Scout never got to see. Perhaps you can witness it for him.

As you leave, the terminal chimes. Inventory change recorded. A second line slowly appears: Next time, ask for the price first. The corridor remains empty. Perhaps Closure knew which drawer you would open all along.
